_comment: Copy this file to map_sources.json to change the map's tile sources.
map_sources.json is gitignored: it may name an environment variable
holding an API key, and it may contain local file paths. A missing or
unreadable file is not an error -- the map falls back to the built-in
list in map_window.py and writes one line to the event log.
Fields: name, type (mbtiles | xyz | wms), url or path, attribution,
min_zoom, max_zoom, optional key_env (NAME of an environment variable
holding the key -- never the key itself), optional key_param (the query
parameter the provider expects it in, default 'key'), and bulk_download
(true only where the provider's terms permit tools/fetch_tiles.py to
NO GOOGLE MAPS OR GOOGLE TILE SERVERS. Google Earth is only the viewer

sources.name: Offline (MBTiles)
_note: Reads every .mbtiles file in this directory, newest match wins.
This is the default whenever a pack exists, because the launch site
has no internet. Build one with tools/fetch_tiles.py, QGIS or Mobile
Atlas Creator -- see the README.

sources.name: ISRO Bhuvan (boundaries only)
_note: VERIFIED from this machine on 2026-10-26: this endpoint answers
anonymously (no token, no registration) and returns real 256 px
EPSG:3857 PNG tiles for several basemap:* layers.
It is a VECTOR server: this layer draws administrative boundaries,
not satellite imagery. The documented 'Bhuvan_satellite' layer does
NOT exist on it, and the imagery hosts were unreachable from here
(bhuvan-ras2 -> HTTP 404, bhuvan-vec2 -> read timeout). See the
README for what was and was not confirmed.
Other layers that answered with real tiles, if you want to try them:
basemap:inida_state_ql_new   (state outlines; spelling is theirs)
basemap:waterbody_DEM        (water bodies)
cadastral:cad_india

sources.name: OpenStreetMap
_note: Light interactive use only. The OSMF Tile Usage Policy forbids bulk
downloading, so tools/fetch_tiles.py refuses this source and says
why. The application sends a User-Agent naming itself, as the policy
requires. For an offline pack, use a provider whose terms allow it,
or render your own from an OSM extract.

sources.name: Sentinel-2 cloudless 2023 (EOX)
sources.attribution: Sentinel-2 cloudless - https://s2maps.eu by EOX IT Services GmbH (Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2023)
_note: Satellite imagery, about 10 m per pixel; past z14 the map overzooms.
CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: NON-COMMERCIAL use only, share alike, attribution
shown whenever the imagery is. EOX permits offline packs inside an
application, not redistribution of the raw tiles -- so the pack is
gitignored and rebuilt locally (see the README).
URL VERIFIED 2026-10-27 from WMTSCapabilities.xml: layer
s2cloudless-2023_3857, TileMatrixSet g, template
.../{TileMatrixSet}/{TileMatrix}/{TileRow}/{TileCol}.jpg, i.e. z, y,
x. Note the y before x. The file says http://, which redirects to
this https:// address.
rate_limit (requests/s) and max_tiles (per job, not liftable with
--force) apply to tools/fetch_tiles.py.

_why_disabled: MapmyIndia / Mappls needs an API key from them and their terms have
NOT been checked for this project. Enable it only after reading
those terms yourself. The key is read from the environment variable
named in key_env and is never stored in this file or in the repo.
Move this entry up into 'sources' and set MAPPLS_API_KEY to use it.
